hints.title: Simplify square roots with absolute values
hints.body: The paired radicals give 1−sin2θ=|cosθ| and 1−cos2θ=|sinθ|.
hints.pitfall: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="prefix">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="true" fence="true" form="postfix">|</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, which need not equal z.
hints.pause: Classify the expression by the signs of sine and cosine.

recall.reminder: A principal square root is nonnegative, so a square underneath produces an absolute value.

hints.title: Work through the sign cases
hints.body: Evaluate the simplified expression when sine and cosine have equal nonzero signs, opposite signs, and when either is zero.
hints.recap: Absolute values must be removed according to the current sign case.
hints.pitfall: Include axis angles separately from the open quadrants.
hints.pause: Identify which sign cases satisfy the equation.

recall.reminder: Absolute values must be removed according to the current sign case.

hints.title: Count the allowed integer angles
hints.body: Translate your successful sign cases into intervals in the stated list. Count each inclusive integer interval using last minus first plus one.
hints.recap: An inclusive count includes both endpoints.
hints.pitfall: Zero degrees is absent from the list; 360 degrees is present.
hints.pause: Derive the intervals, check overlaps at boundaries, and total the permitted values.

recall.reminder: An inclusive count includes both endpoints.

solution:
The expression simplifies to sinθ|cosθ|+cosθ|sinθ|. It is zero exactly when sine and cosine have opposite signs or at least one is zero. Equal nonzero signs make the two terms share a sign and prevent cancellation.

Among the stated integer angles, this gives [90∘, 180∘] and [270∘, 360∘]. Each inclusive block contains 91 integers, so the total is 182.

Answer F: 182.
knowledgePattern: Convert square-root products to absolute values and count inclusive angles
